message.content:
Search this repository for code related to "memo" metadata that is derived/computed from memo content (not set by the user). This would be metadata used for lists/previews — things like snippets, titles extracted from content, character counts, etc. Look for:

1. Functions or methods that compute/extract metadata from memo content
2. The triggers that cause recomputation (create, update, etc.)
3. What properties are extracted

Search breadth: very thorough. Look in directories related to memos, stores, services, API handlers. Try patterns like "memo" combined with "metadata", "snippet", "extract", "compute", "derive", "preview", "property", "title". Also check for any memo-related protobuf definitions that distinguish between user-set and computed fields.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

24	func (v Visibility) String() string {
25		switch v {
26		case Public:
27			return "PUBLIC"
28		case Protected:
29			return "PROTECTED"
30		default:
31			return "PRIVATE"
32		}
33	}

35	type Memo struct {
36		// ID is the system generated unique identifier for the memo.
37		ID int32
38		// UID is the user defined unique identifier for the memo.
39		UID string
40	
41		// Standard fields
42		RowStatus RowStatus
43		CreatorID int32
44		CreatedTs int64

46	
47		// Domain specific fields

58		ID  *int32
59		UID *string

61		IDList  []int32
62		UIDList []string
63	
64		// Standard fields
65		RowStatus *RowStatus
66		CreatorID *int32
67	
68		// Domain specific fields
69		VisibilityList  []Visibility
70		ExcludeContent  bool

79		OrderByPinned    bool

86		TagSearch          []string
87		HasLink            bool
88		HasTaskList        bool
89		HasCode            bool
90		HasIncompleteTasks bool
91	}
92	
93	type UpdateMemo struct {
94		ID         int32
95		UID        *string
96		CreatedTs  *int64
97		UpdatedTs  *int64
98		RowStatus  *RowStatus
99		Content    *string
100		Visibility *Visibility
101		Pinned     *bool
102		Payload    *storepb.MemoPayload

106		ID int32

109	func (s *Store) CreateMemo(ctx context.Context, create *Memo) (*Memo, error) {
110		if !base.UIDMatcher.MatchString(create.UID) {
111			return nil, errors.New("invalid uid")
112		}
113		return s.driver.CreateMemo(ctx, create)
114	}

117		return s.driver.ListMemos(ctx, find)
118	}

120	func (s *Store) GetMemo(ctx context.Context, find *FindMemo) (*Memo, error) {
121		list, err := s.ListMemos(ctx, find)
122		if err != nil {
123			return nil, err
124		}
125		if len(list) == 0 {
126			return nil, nil
127		}
128	
129		memo := list[0]
130		return memo, nil
131	}
132	
133	func (s *Store) UpdateMemo(ctx context.Context, update *UpdateMemo) error {
134		if update.UID != nil && !base.UIDMatcher.MatchString(*update.UID) {
135			return errors.New("invalid uid")
136		}
137		return s.driver.UpdateMemo(ctx, update)
138	}
139	
140	func (s *Store) DeleteMemo(ctx context.Context, delete *DeleteMemo) error {
141		// Clean up memo_relation records where this memo is either the source or target.
142		if err := s.driver.DeleteMemoRelation(ctx, &DeleteMemoRelation{MemoID: &delete.ID}); err != nil {
143			return err
144		}
145		if err := s.driver.DeleteMemoRelation(ctx, &DeleteMemoRelation{RelatedMemoID: &delete.ID}); err != nil {
146			return err
147		}
148		// Clean up attachments linked to this memo.
149		attachments, err := s.ListAttachments(ctx, &FindAttachment{MemoID: &delete.ID})
150		if err != nil {
151			return err
152		}
153		for _, attachment := range attachments {
154			if err := s.DeleteAttachment(ctx, &DeleteAttachment{ID: attachment.ID}); err != nil {
155				return err
156			}
157		}
158		return s.driver.DeleteMemo(ctx, delete)
159	}

67		// policy, used by both the gRPC-Gateway middleware and the Connect interceptor.
68		authorizer := NewAuthorizer(s.Store, s.Secret, s.Profile)
69		gatewayAuthMiddleware := func(next runtime.HandlerFunc) runtime.HandlerFunc {
70			return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, pathParams map[string]string) {
71				ctx := r.Context()
72	
73				// The RPC method name is set by grpc-gateway after routing. When it can't be
74				// determined, skip the policy check and let the service layer handle visibility.
75				rpcMethod, ok := runtime.RPCMethod(ctx)
76				authHeader := r.Header.Get("Authorization")
77	
78				result := authorizer.Authenticate(ctx, authHeader)
79				if ok {
80					if err := authorizer.CheckAccess(ctx, rpcMethod, result); err != nil {

91				next(w, r, pathParams)
92			}
93		}

113		}
114		if err := v1pb.RegisterAIServiceHandlerServer(ctx, gwMux, s); err != nil {

116		}

153	func (s *Server) startBackgroundRunners(ctx context.Context) {
154		// Create a separate context for each background runner
155		// This allows us to control cancellation for each runner independently
156		s3Context, s3Cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
157	
158		// Store the cancel function so we can properly shut down runners
159		s.backgroundRunnerCancels = append(s.backgroundRunnerCancels, s3Cancel)
160	
161		// Create and start S3 presign runner
162		s3presignRunner := s3presign.NewRunner(s.Store)
163		s3presignRunner.RunOnce(ctx)
164	
165		// Start continuous S3 presign runner
166		s.backgroundRunnerWG.Add(1)
167		go func() {
168			defer s.backgroundRunnerWG.Done()
169			s3presignRunner.Run(s3Context)
170			slog.Info("s3presign runner stopped")
171		}()
172	
173		slog.Info("background runners started")
174	}

176	func (s *Server) stopBackgroundRunners() {
177		for _, cancelFunc := range s.backgroundRunnerCancels {
178			if cancelFunc != nil {
179				cancelFunc()
180			}
181		}
182	}

11	func (*APIV1Service) parseMemoOrderBy(orderBy string, memoFind *store.FindMemo) error {
12		if strings.TrimSpace(orderBy) == "" {
13			return errors.New("empty order_by")
14		}
15	
16		// Split by comma to support multiple sort fields per AIP-132.
17		fields := strings.Split(orderBy, ",")
18	
19		// Track if we've seen pinned field.
20		hasPinned := false
21		hasExplicitTimeField := false
22	
23		for _, field := range fields {
24			parts := strings.Fields(strings.TrimSpace(field))
25			if len(parts) == 0 {
26				continue
27			}
28	
29			fieldName := parts[0]
30			fieldDirection := "desc" // default per AIP-132 (we use desc as default for time fields)
31			if len(parts) > 1 {
32				fieldDirection = strings.ToLower(parts[1])
33				if fieldDirection != "asc" && fieldDirection != "desc" {
34					return errors.Errorf("invalid order direction: %s, must be 'asc' or 'desc'", parts[1])
35				}
36			}
37	
38			switch fieldName {
39			case "pinned":
40				hasPinned = true
41				memoFind.OrderByPinned = true
42				// Note: pinned is always DESC (true first) regardless of direction specified.
43			case "create_time", "name":
44				// Only set if this is the first time field we encounter.
45				if !hasExplicitTimeField {
46					memoFind.OrderByTimeAsc = fieldDirection == "asc"
47				}
48				hasExplicitTimeField = true
49			case "update_time":
50				// Only set if this is the first time field we encounter.
51				if !hasExplicitTimeField {
52					memoFind.OrderByUpdatedTs = true
53					memoFind.OrderByTimeAsc = fieldDirection == "asc"
54				}
55				hasExplicitTimeField = true
56			default:
57				return errors.Errorf("unsupported order field: %s, supported fields are: pinned, create_time, update_time, name", fieldName)
58			}
59		}
60	
61		// If only pinned was specified, still need to set a default time ordering.
62		if hasPinned && !memoFind.OrderByUpdatedTs && len(fields) == 1 {
63			memoFind.OrderByTimeAsc = false // default to desc

Here is my complete report on computed/derived memo metadata in this codebase.

---

## Computed/Derived Memo Metadata

### 1. What Properties Are Extracted

Two categories of metadata are derived from memo content:

**A. Stored Payload Properties (persisted in the database)**

Defined in the protobuf at `/bench/repo/proto/store/memo.proto` (lines 7-29), inside `MemoPayload.Property`:

- `has_link` (bool) -- whether the memo content contains any markdown link
- `has_task_list` (bool) -- whether the memo contains any GFM task checkboxes
- `has_code` (bool) -- whether the memo contains code blocks or inline code spans
- `has_incomplete_tasks` (bool) -- whether any task checkboxes are unchecked
- `title` (string) -- plain text extracted from the first block-level H1 heading, if the very first block-level child of the document is an `# H1`

Also extracted and stored in the payload:
- `tags` (repeated string) -- all `#tag` occurrences found in the content (deduplicated, case-preserved)

These are stored in the `MemoPayload` field of the `store.Memo` struct (`/bench/repo/store/memo.go`, line 51).

**B. On-the-fly Computed Fields (not persisted, generated at response time)**

Defined in the API protobuf at `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto` (lines 266-267):

- `snippet` (string) -- a plain-text summary of the memo content, max 64 characters, with markdown formatting stripped, code blocks removed, and truncation at word boundaries

The snippet is generated each time a memo is converted from storage to API response. It is NOT stored in the database.

### 2. Functions/Methods That Compute the Metadata

**Core extraction engine:** `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go`

- `ExtractAll()` (line 356) -- the primary single-pass extraction function. Parses markdown via goldmark, walks the AST once, and collects: tags, mentions, and all Property fields (has_link, has_task_list, has_code, has_incomplete_tasks, title). Returns an `ExtractedData` struct (defined at line 21).

- `ExtractProperties()` (line 193) -- standalone property extraction (same logic as ExtractAll but without tags/mentions). Used in tests but the production path prefers `ExtractAll`.

- `ExtractTags()` (line 143) -- standalone tag extraction.

- `GenerateSnippet()` (line 264) -- creates a plain-text summary. Walks the AST, collects text nodes, skips code blocks, adds spaces between block elements, and truncates at a word boundary. Called with a max length of 64 characters in production.

- `extractHeadingText()` (line 173) -- helper that extracts plain text (stripping inline formatting) from a heading node, used for the `title` property.

**Payload rebuild function:** `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`

- `RebuildMemoPayload()` (line 74) -- calls `markdownService.ExtractAll()` on the memo's content and stores the result in `memo.Payload.Tags` and `memo.Payload.Property`.

**Snippet generation at API layer:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`

- `getMemoContentSnippet()` (line 83) -- calls `s.MarkdownService.GenerateSnippet(content, 64)`.

**Store-to-API conversion:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go`

- `convertMemoFromStoreWithCreators()` (line 31) -- the central conversion function. It copies `Tags`, `Property`, and `Location` from the stored payload (line 48-51), calls `getMemoContentSnippet()` to generate the snippet (line 76-82), and populates the API `Memo.Snippet` field.

- `convertMemoPropertyFromStore()` (line 315) -- maps stored `MemoPayload_Property` to API `Memo_Property`.

### 3. Triggers for Recomputation

**On CreateMemo:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, line 108
```go
if err := memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, create, s.MarkdownService); err != nil {
```
Called before `s.Store.CreateMemo()`. The payload (tags + properties) is computed and persisted with the new memo.

**On UpdateMemo (when content changes):** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, line 447
```go
if err := memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload(ctx, memo, s.MarkdownService); err != nil {
```
Called only when the `"content"` field is in the update mask. The rebuilt payload is saved via `update.Payload = memo.Payload`.

**Batch rebuild (Runner.RunOnce):** `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`, line 27
The `RunOnce()` method iterates through ALL memos in batches of 100 and rebuilds each payload. However, this runner is NOT currently invoked at server startup (the startup runner code at `/bench/repo/server/server.go` line 153 only starts the S3 presign runner). The `RunOnce` function exists for manual or migration use.

**Snippet generation is NOT a trigger** -- snippets are computed on-the-fly every time a memo is serialized to an API response (in `convertMemoFromStoreWithCreators` and in `batchConvertMemoRelations` for relation snippets).

### 4. Protobuf Distinction Between User-Set and Computed Fields

In `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto`, the `Memo` message clearly marks computed fields:

- `tags` (field 10): `OUTPUT_ONLY` -- extracted from content by the server
- `property` (field 15): `OUTPUT_ONLY` -- "The computed properties of the memo"
- `snippet` (field 17): `OUTPUT_ONLY` -- "The snippet of the memo content. Plain text only."
- `reactions` (field 14): `OUTPUT_ONLY`
- `creator` (field 3): `OUTPUT_ONLY`
- `parent` (field 16): `OUTPUT_ONLY`

User-settable fields are marked `REQUIRED` or `OPTIONAL`:
- `content` (field 7): `REQUIRED`
- `visibility` (field 9): `REQUIRED`
- `pinned` (field 11): `OPTIONAL`
- `location` (field 18): `OPTIONAL`
- `attachments` (field 12): `OPTIONAL`
- `relations` (field 13): `OPTIONAL`

The store-level protobuf (`/bench/repo/proto/store/memo.proto`) has a comment on line 14: "The calculated properties from the memo content." for the `Property` message inside `MemoPayload`.

### 5. Frontend Usage of Computed Metadata

- **Snippet** is used in: memo lists (`UserMemoMap`, line 154), comment previews (`MemoCommentListView.tsx`, line 45), relation cards (`RelationCard.tsx`, line 12), and the memo detail sidebar (`MemoDetailSidebar.tsx`, line 155).

- **Property fields** (hasLink, hasTaskList, hasCode) are used as filter criteria in `/bench/repo/web/src/contexts/MemoFilterContext.tsx` (lines 11-13) and displayed as filter chips in `/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoFilters.tsx` (lines 45-56). The frontend maps these to CEL filter expressions like `has_link`, `has_task_list`, `has_code` in `/bench/repo/web/src/hooks/useMemoFilters.ts` (lines 73-78).

- **Shortcuts** reference these property fields for pre-built filters in `/bench/repo/web/src/pages/Shortcuts.tsx` (lines 78, 84, 166-169).

### Key File Paths Summary

| Purpose | File |
|---|---|
| Store protobuf (MemoPayload, Property) | `/bench/repo/proto/store/memo.proto` |
| API protobuf (Memo, Property, snippet) | `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto` |
| Markdown extraction engine | `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go` |
| Markdown extraction tests | `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown_test.go` |
| Payload rebuild function | `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` |
| Create/Update memo (triggers rebuild) | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` |
| Store-to-API converter (snippet gen) | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go` |
| Snippet helper (64-char limit) | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go` |
| Store model (Memo, FindMemoPayload) | `/bench/repo/store/memo.go` |
| Frontend filter context | `/bench/repo/web/src/contexts/MemoFilterContext.tsx` |
| Frontend filter display | `/bench/repo/web/src/components/MemoFilters.tsx` |
| Frontend filter-to-CEL mapping | `/bench/repo/web/src/hooks/useMemoFilters.ts` |
